reason: Attacked and held, and the locator can be sharpened. I read the Gutenberg transcription named in the evidence (59432, whose front matter shows the Small, Maynard and Company title page, the 1920 copyright line and the contents with TRIFLES first at page 1), and then, because that transcription carries no pagination, I also downloaded the page images text of the 1920 copyright-deposit copy on archive.org (plays00glas, plays00glas_djvu.txt). Both give the speech word for word: I might have known she needed help! I know how things can be for women. I tell you, it's queer, Mrs. Peters. We live close together and we live far apart. We all go through the same things it's all just a different kind of the same thing. The scan's running heads place it on page 27 of the 30 pages Trifles occupies, about two pages before the curtain, which confirms near the close and supplies the page the citation was missing. Speaker Mrs. Hale, correctly named; she is answering Mrs. Peters. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, Glaspell banned=false, none of three. Scope: a one act play first performed 1916 and printed here in 1920, no scripture, no lyric, and although the play turns on a killing the quotation itself carries no wound or death and needs no warning. Source line is 106 characters, leads with Glaspell, no em dash, no straight quote, speaker in parentheses after the locator; Drama is the form. Two caveats short of refutation: the 1920 book sets the dash spaced ( ) where the card closes it up, which is typographic normalization and not a change of wording; and the card's parenthesis names the 1920 volume, which is the edition the wording matches but not the play's first appearance in print (1916), so a reader could take 1920 for the date of the work. Adding the page, as below, is the improvement worth making.
